title: Improve menu image loading speed on mobile data

requirements.text: Optimize the Menu page screenshot image loading for mobile users on slow/mobile data by reducing bytes transferred and prioritizing above-the-fold menu screenshot rendering.

quotes: I opened the website in mobile but the images of menu wont load up rapidly under mobile data

acceptanceCriteria: On the /menu page, the first visible menu screenshot uses high fetch priority (e.g., eager load / fetchpriority=high) so it starts downloading immediately when the page is opened.
Menu screenshot assets used on mobile are smaller/optimized versions (reduced dimensions and/or compression) compared to the current originals, while preserving acceptable readability.
MENU_SCREENSHOT_ASSETS is updated to reference the optimized screenshot asset URLs (or uses responsive selection that serves optimized assets on mobile).
The UI continues to show a clear loading state while the image loads and degrades gracefully if an image fails to load (no broken layout).

requirements.text: Add resource hints to improve perceived performance for menu screenshots on mobile by preloading the first menu screenshot on the Menu page (or at the document level) without breaking other pages.

quotes: images of menu wont load up rapidly under mobile data

acceptanceCriteria: The app includes a preload hint for the first menu screenshot (the first entry in MENU_SCREENSHOT_ASSETS) targeted for mobile viewports where appropriate.
Preload does not introduce console errors or duplicate/conflicting resource hints in the document head.

constraints: Do not edit any files under frontend/src/components/ui or any paths listed in frontend.immutablePaths (compose existing components instead).
Keep all changes within the existing single-frontend React app; no new backend services or external CDNs.
nonGoals: Do not add new menu features (e.g., ordering flow, new menu sections, real-time updates).
Do not implement third-party image CDNs or external image optimization services.
